summary: Daniel B. Stevenson, a scholar of Buddhist studies and Sinology, earned his Ph.D. from Columbia University. He held positions at Butler University (attested 1986), the University of Kansas (attested 1996–2003), and served as a Guest Scholar at Soka University.

Daniel Baum is a linguist and Indologist who studied at the Hebrew University of Jerusalem and Leiden University. He was taught by Saul Migron and completed his doctoral work under the supervision of Alexander Lubotsky (~2001–2006).
Daniel Borengasser is a scholar in history, archaeology, and Japanology. He earned a Master of Arts degree at the University of Oregon under the supervision of Akiko Walley.

Daniel Boucher specializes in Buddhist studies and Sinology. He studied at Indiana University Bloomington and the University of Pennsylvania under Victor H. Mair, Ludo Rocher, and Gregory Schopen, and served as Associate Professor at Cornell University (attested 2000–2008, 2026).

Daniel Clarke Waugh works in history, archaeology, and Iranian and Central Asian studies. He studied physics at Yale and completed graduate work at Harvard University before taking up a post at the University of Washington in 1972.

Daniel Coit Gilman studied at Yale, Harvard, Cambridge, and Berlin. He served as Yale's librarian (1856–1872), president of the University of California (1872–1875), founding president of Johns Hopkins University (1875–1901), and president of the Carnegie Institution for Science (1902–1904).

Daniel Cozort specializes in Buddhist studies, Tibetology, and religious studies. He completed his Ph.D. at the University of Virginia under Jeffrey Hopkins, also studying under several traditional Tibetan teachers, and held posts at Bates College and Dickinson College.

Daniel Dubuisson is a scholar of religious studies, history, archaeology, and Indology. He held posts at the Centre national de la recherche scientifique as director of research (~1981–2015) and at Charles de Gaulle University – Lille III.

Daniel Franz Schauffelberger was an Indologist and linguist. He studied at the University of Tübingen (~1838–1841) and Martin Luther University of Halle-Wittenberg (~1841–1843) before completing his Ph.D. at the University of Bonn (~1843–1845).

Daniel H. H. Ingalls was an Indologist and philosopher who earned his degrees at Harvard University and studied under Walter Eugene Clark and Kalipada Tarkacharya. He served as a faculty member at Harvard University from 1938 to 1983.

Daniel John Gogerly was an Indologist and Buddhist studies scholar. He headed the Wesleyan Mission Press (~1818–1823), served as General Superintendent of the Wesleyan Mission in South Ceylon (1838), and held leadership roles in the Royal Asiatic Society of Sri Lanka.

Daniel L. Overmyer was a scholar of Sinology and religious studies who completed his doctorate at the University of Chicago under Philip A. Kuhn. He was a professor at the University of British Columbia (~1970–2001) and held several visiting professorships.

Daniel M. Neuman is an Indologist who studied at the University of Illinois Urbana-Champaign and the University of Chicago. He held academic posts at Dartmouth College (1971–1980), the University of Washington (1980–1995), and UCLA (1995–2018).

Daniel M. Stuart works in Buddhist studies and Indology. After degrees from Pacific Union College, UC Riverside, and UC Berkeley, he held posts at the University of South Carolina (attested 2017) and the University of Hamburg (attested 2026).
Daniel P. Brown worked in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He studied under Geshe Wangyal and served as a professor at Harvard University from approximately 1983 to 2021.
Daniel R. Tuzzeo is a scholar of Buddhist studies and religious studies who completed his thesis at Florida State University, advised by Jimmy Yu, Bryan J. Cuevas, and Joseph Hellweg.

Daniel Schlumberger was an archaeologist and historian educated at the universities of Strasbourg and Paris. He served as Inspector for antiquities in the Levant (1929–1940), Professor at Strasbourg (1955), and held a post at Princeton University (~1958–1969).

Daniel Sperber is a scholar of history, archaeology, and Indology. He studied at University College London (~1963–1968) and held academic posts at Bar-Ilan University (starting ~1968) and the Open University of Israel.

Daniel Stuart Capper, a scholar of religious and Buddhist studies, studied at the University of Virginia and the University of Chicago. He was a professor at the University of Southern Mississippi (2000–2022) and an adjunct at MSU Denver (2023).

Daniel Timothy Aitken works in philosophy, Buddhist studies, and Tibetology. He earned his PhD at the University of Tasmania, having studied under Parimal G. Patil, Leonard van der Kuijp, and Jay L. Garfield.
